architecture.approach: Extend the existing NestJS auth module into a tenancy-aware authority. A new tenancy layer (organizations, clinics, user_memberships) separates global identity from per-clinic membership. The access token carries org_id, clinic_id and role resolved from the active membership, and a request-scoped tenant context is built only from the verified token so no request body can widen scope. Redis becomes required infrastructure for security state (lockout counters and the refresh-token blacklist) under a strict, fail-closed mode, while ordinary caching keeps its in-memory fallback. Registration, invitation, workspace switching and auditing are added as services behind the existing guards and the global validation pipe.

components.name: auth module
components.description: Adds register, switch-workspace, invitation and tenancy-aware token issuance alongside the existing login, refresh, logout and password routes.

components.name: tenancy module
components.description: Owns organizations, clinics, memberships, invitations and their services and DTOs.

components.name: audit module
components.description: Owns the transactional audit writer and the append-only audit log.

components.name: tenant context provider
components.description: Request-scoped holder populated exclusively from the verified token, read by every scoped query.

components.name: RedisCacheService
components.description: Adds a strict mode and atomic counter operations used by security paths; keeps the degraded in-memory path for caching only.

components.name: token blacklist store
components.description: Redis-backed revocation store keyed by token hash with TTL equal to the token remaining life.

components.name: login attempt store
components.description: Redis-backed atomic failure counter with TTL backing the lockout policy.

components.name: RolesGuard
components.description: Reads the active role from the membership claim instead of the user record.

components.name: JWT strategy
components.description: Validates the tenancy claims and rejects tokens whose membership is no longer active.

components.name: mail module
components.description: Adds invitation and password-reset templates in EN, AR and FR.

components.name: backoffice auth pages
components.description: Adds the registration wizard, accept-invitation screen, workspace switcher and staff directory.

components.name: i18n catalogues
components.description: Adds auth strings for EN, AR and FR in both front ends.

components.name: docker-compose
components.description: Adds the Redis service the security state depends on.

components.name: registration entry points
components.description: Retires the pending-approval self-signup so /register is the only public self-service path, and establishes the owner session as registration completes.

dataModel.flowDescription: A registration request opens one transaction that creates the identity, the organization, the first clinic and a SUPER_ADMIN membership, then issues a scoped token. Login verifies the argon2 hash, consults the Redis failure counter and lockout expiry, resolves the active membership, and issues an access token carrying org_id, clinic_id and role plus a rotating refresh token whose hash is stored and whose revocation is mirrored into the Redis blacklist. Switching workspace verifies an active membership for the requested clinic and re-issues a scoped token, rotating the refresh token for the new scope. Invitations are stored as a hashed single-use token; acceptance consumes it and grants exactly the recorded membership. Every create, update and delete writes an audit row inside the same transaction as the mutation.

securityConsiderations.description: Global Helmet headers remain applied; nothing in this feature disables CSP or HSTS on auth routes.
A stricter named throttler is applied to login, register, forgot-password, reset-password and accept-invite, on top of the existing global limit.
Every new endpoint has a class-validator DTO; the global ValidationPipe with whitelist and forbidNonWhitelisted rejects unknown fields.
All tenant filtering is expressed as Prisma query constraints; no raw SQL is introduced.
No dangerouslySetInnerHTML in auth UI; email templates escape interpolated names.
Auth state changes stay POST behind the explicit CORS allow-list with credentials enabled.
New keys are documented in .env.example only; no real values are committed.
The refresh cookie Secure attribute derives from configuration and must be true outside local development.
Login lockout fails closed: when Redis cannot be reached the attempt is rejected rather than permitted, so an outage cannot disable brute-force protection.
The audit log is append-only from the application perspective; no endpoint updates or deletes audit rows.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: Login keeps a constant number of round trips: one indexed membership lookup, one Redis counter operation and one argon2 verification, with the argon2 cost left at its current setting.
Membership lookups are indexed on (userId, status) and (clinicId, status) so the guard and the workspace switcher resolve scope without table scans.
Audit writes add no extra round trip because they participate in the mutation transaction.

risks.description: Removing the clinic-scoped role from users touches RolesGuard, the JWT strategy and the seed script simultaneously.
risks.mitigation: Ship the data migration and the seed update in the same change as the model update, and keep the four existing dev logins working (T2.3, T2.4).

risks.description: A fail-closed lockout makes Redis a single point of failure for login.
risks.mitigation: Health-check Redis at startup, surface a clear retryable error rather than a generic failure, and document the operational dependency (T1.2, T5.5).

risks.description: The public register route can be abused to create organizations.
risks.mitigation: Per-endpoint rate limiting plus the restriction that public registration can never join an existing clinic (T6.6, T4.1).

risks.description: Existing clients depend on the current unversioned auth routes.
risks.mitigation: Route paths are retained and the versioning decision is documented in Swagger (T6.7).
